title: Mistake #2: why your screws keep splitting the wood

slides.title: Why did that board just crack?
slides.sub: One skipped step splits the wood

slides.label: Mistake #2
slides.heading: Driving screws without a pilot hole
slides.body: A screw pushes wood fibers apart as it goes in. Close to the end or edge of a board there isn't enough wood to hold that pressure, so it splits. Hardwood and thin trim split even faster.

slides.label: The fix
slides.heading: Pre-drill a pilot hole
slides.body: Drill a hole about the size of the screw's solid core, not the threads. The threads still bite, but the wood has room. Add a countersink so the head sits flush.
slides.fix: Hold the bit next to the screw: you should still see the threads.

slides.heading: 3 quick checks
items: Stay at least 1" from the end of the board.
Clamp the parts so they can't shift.
Drive slowly. Stop when the head is flush.
